desc: Join this machine to a NetBird network on NetBird Cloud or your own management server
authLink: Open this link to authenticate the device
authCode: If the login page asks for a code, enter:
authHelp: On macOS and Windows the login usually has to be completed in a browser on this machine; use a setup key when managing it remotely. The link is renewed automatically when it expires.
notConnected: Not connected to the network yet
idleHint: Idle peers have no connection right now: with lazy connections (on by default in the dashboard) traffic to them sets one up automatically; offline peers also show as idle.
setupKeyPlaceholder: Setup key (leave empty to authenticate with a login link)
setupKeyHelp: Create one on the Setup Keys page of the management dashboard; suited to unattended devices
managementUrlHelp: Leave empty for NetBird Cloud; enter your own management server when self-hosting
hostnamePlaceholder: Leave empty to use the system hostname
acceptRoutesHelp: Use the network routes from the management server to reach networks behind other routing peers
serverRoutesHelp: Allow forwarding the networks and exit traffic the management server assigns to this machine; networks and exit nodes are configured in the dashboard
acceptDnsHelp: Use the DNS settings from the management server
blockInboundHelp: Reject all inbound connections from the network, overriding the access policies of the management server
manageDaemonHelp: When off, the NetBird service already installed on the system is used and only netbird up is run
userspaceHelp: No TUN device or privileges needed; recommended in containers
localForwardingHelp: Let other peers reach services on this machine through its network address, including services listening only on 127.0.0.1; access policies of the management server still apply
socks5Help: With userspace networking, local programs reach devices in the network through this proxy
socks5Public: This proxy has no authentication. When it listens on a non-local address, any device that can reach that address can use it to enter the network; listening on 127.0.0.1 only is recommended
wgPortHelp: 0 uses the default 51820; allow this UDP port in the firewall for direct connections
daemonArgsPlaceholder: Appended to netbird service run, e.g. --log-level=debug
envPlaceholder: One KEY=VALUE per line, e.g. NB_DISABLE_USERSPACE_ROUTING=true
envHelp: Passed to the daemon; use them for the advanced NB_ options in the NetBird docs
daemonAddrPlaceholder: Empty for the system default, e.g. unix:///var/run/netbird.sock
noInstances: No instances yet. Add one to join this machine to a NetBird network on NetBird Cloud or your own management server
confirmDelete: Delete this instance? A managed instance using the default state directory logs out first (removing this machine from the network) and its login state and keys are deleted; a custom state directory is kept.
namePlaceholder: e.g. home or office; empty uses the management server's domain
kernelHelp: Kernel mode needs a TUN device and root privileges; NetBird kernel mode uses a fixed routing table and firewall rules, so only one kernel-mode instance can be enabled at a time. Turn on userspace networking for the others
stateDirPlaceholder: Empty uses netbird/<instance key> under the config directory
stateDirHelp: Stores the login state and WireGuard keys. Enter an existing state directory (for example /var/lib/netbird mounted by an earlier NetBird container) to keep the peer without registering again; instances cannot share one
daemonAddrManagedPlaceholder: Empty uses netbird.sock in the state directory
confirmLogout: Log this instance out? This machine's peer is removed from the network, and joining again requires logging in again or a setup key.
